claim: Scenario response generation uses one bounded provider-neutral contract, works through the optional local model or native-approved remote APIs, and commits only attributed output against the exact selected-scenario revision.
verified: The provider receives a detached bounded snapshot of only the selected scenario
Local generation uses the configured loopback endpoint and selected local model
Turning local AI off prevents local invocation without disabling manual scenarios or API selection
OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and xAI routes reuse the Rust-owned credential and native Send once boundary
Provider output must match contract version, run, provider, and requested-model route
Ambient fields, control bytes, oversized content, route substitution, and malformed output fail before shared mutation
A scenario edit during generation makes commit fail closed without adding a response
Successful output enters the existing collaborative response graph with provider, executed model, and run provenance
Two independent variants from the same source revision remain separate responses
The product keeps manual, local, and API paths explicit and does not claim generated text changed policy
Production TypeScript and Vite build passes
limitations: No live paid-provider call or packaged pointer/keyboard interaction is included in this proof.
Remote API results pass the native one-shot disclosure boundary, but the shared response stores only provider/model/run identity rather than the complete content-free provider-run record.
Generated variants can be inspected but do not yet have a product editing/regeneration workflow; P-17 remains planned.
Generation does not apply policy text, score model quality, or prove superiority over another research product.
